name: Never flow analysis requires static branch typing

input.source_text: mut x: Integer = if true { 1 } else { "text" }

applicability.reason: Supported. C083 makes branch RESULT analysis treat `Never` as bottom: a branch that can only raise contributes no value Type to the enclosing expression. The analyser did not model an `if` at all, so no branch contributed anything and nothing could be checked; it now unions the branches that CAN produce a value and drops a diverging one. `if c { 1 } else { raise :e }` therefore stays Integer-typed and is admitted, while this row's `\"text\"` branch contributes an incompatible Type and is refused - which is what shows the branch Type is genuinely computed rather than skipped. D-458's half already held: a callable promising `Never` and completing normally is rejected.
